sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the souls of Yisrael originate in the supernal thought, which is beyond even the level of thought within thought.

translations.translation: However, who are those who contemplate and serve in this state of self-nullification?
This is as the verse says, "Shema Yisrael,"
for Yisrael ascended in thought.
And the explanation of "Yisrael ascended in thought" is that it refers to supernal thought,
which is above the level of thought as it comes in a limited form.
That is to say, not only is it higher in level than the thought that is in speech and the speech that is in thought,
but it is also above the level of thought within thought.
For,
the thought that is in speech is what one thinks about how to speak,
that is, how to explain the particular modes of speech,
and this is not the true essence of thought,
for it is the aspect of thought as it is clothed in the matter of speech,
thinking about how to speak.
And the speech that is in thought is the thought itself, which is above the matter of speech,
but nevertheless it includes speech,
as mentioned above regarding the greatness of speech, that it is the single thought that includes the particulars of speech.
And the true essence of thought is the aspect of thought within thought,
which is like thinking the essence of the intellect before it is clothed in letters,
which is higher in level than the aspect of the intellect after it is clothed in letters.
And the superiority of the intellect before it is clothed in letters over the aspect of the intellect after it is clothed in letters is in two matters.
The first,
that the intellect that is clothed in letters is already depicted in the particular modes of explanation,
which are the letters in which it is clothed,
for the letters are the particular modes of the explanation of the intellect,
but before it is clothed in letters it is not yet depicted in the particular modes of explanation,
and therefore it can be explained in several different ways.
And the second,
that the intellect before it is clothed in letters,
not only is it not depicted in the particular modes of explanation,
but furthermore,
even the intellect itself is in a state of simplicity,
being still abstracted from the particulars of the intellect itself
(not only from the modes of explanation).
However, the aspect of "Yisrael ascended in thought" is the aspect of supernal thought, which is above even the aspect of thought within thought,
for the aspect of thought within thought is still in a state of form,
for although it is devoid of modes and particulars,
nevertheless it is at least in the form of intellect,
but supernal thought is in absolute simplicity.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the soul descends from its high root in supernal thought to this low world, and answers that the descent is for the sake of an ascent to an even higher level.

translations.translation: However, according to this, it must be understood why the soul descended below,
for this is a descent from a high roof to a deep pit
literally,
since the root of the souls is in supernal thought,
then for what benefit did it descend below?
But the explanation is,
that this descent is for the sake of an ascent,
and the ascent is to a level that is above even the aspect of supernal thought.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section cites a Talmudic contradiction about gathering grain versus strangers tending flocks, resolved by the Maggid that lacking the service of "with all your might" renders it as not doing His will.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
for it is stated in the Gemara,
One verse says,
"And you shall gather your grain,"
and another verse says,
"And strangers shall stand and tend your flocks,"
Here, when Israel does the will of the Omnipresent,
there, when they do not do the will of the Omnipresent.
And the difficulty in this is known,
for the verse "And you shall gather your grain" is stated in the portion of "Vehayah Im Shamoa,"
in which it is said,
"And it will be, if you surely listen... with all your heart and with all your soul,"
so how can it be said about this that it is when they do not do the will of the Omnipresent?
And the Maggid answered,
that since the service is only "with all your heart and with all your soul,"
but the service of "with all your might" is lacking,
therefore it is called "not doing the will of the Omnipresent."
